title: Inputs and Outputs
summary: How a parent component talks to a child, and the child talks back.
heading: Inputs and Outputs

blocks.text: Components are nested, so they need to share. A parent passes data down to a child through an input, and a child sends events up to the parent through an output.

blocks.caption: Data flows down through inputs; events flow up through outputs.

blocks.text: Inside the child, declare an input(). It becomes a signal, so you read it by calling it with ().

blocks.label: greeting.ts (child)

blocks.text: The parent sets the input with property binding — the same [ ] from the last chapter.
The child declares an output() and calls .emit(...) to send a value up when something happens.

blocks.label: like-button.ts (child)

blocks.text: The parent listens with event binding — the same ( ) from the last chapter.
Inputs and outputs connect two components, so they need a real Angular app to run — try them in your own project with ng serve.

items: Data flows down via input(); events flow up via output().
An input is a signal — read it with name().
The parent sets an input with [name]="value".
A child fires an output with thing.emit(value).
